title: A cut with no publish.url stamps the version after the candidate's tests, so it tags a commit nothing has tested and re-runs the suite on it
body:
## Summary

**A cut with no `release.publish.url` tags a commit that nothing has tested, so every release re-runs the whole suite.** The release core makes the release commit (the version bump and the CHANGELOG date) at cut time, after every test run on the candidate. Its `gates` step then runs `check all` and `test all` on that commit locally, and its `ci` step waits for the CI run that the tag push triggers. The commit that passed is never the commit that ships.

hv, 2026-10-30, in intent-vc's session, while Gtools 0.8.3's `ci` step waited: "I really don't get why this is done twice. Why don't we just remember the hash that worked and set the release tag to that hash? It feels like we run the same damn test suite four or fives times per release ... it's utterly insane."

## Measured: Gtools 0.8.3, 2026-10-30

The full suite ran five times, for two commits that differ only in a version string and a date:

- On the candidate, 41c283a8: GitHub's workflow_dispatch run 41127185022 (Gtools' macOS job runs only on a tag or a dispatch), kovacs (Ubuntu 26.04, aarch64) and gyges (macOS).
- On the release commit, 79c9233d (VERSION and native/rust/Cargo.toml from 0.8.2 to 0.8.3, Cargo.lock, the CHANGELOG date): the cut's `gates` step on rhadamanth (868 suite tests and the app's 123), then the tag's CI run 41135649951.
- GitHub also ran CI twice on 79c9233d, two seconds apart: run 41135646272 for the push to main and run 41135649951 for the tag push. Their Linux jobs ran the same tests twice.

The tested commit cannot simply be tagged as it stands. It says 0.8.2, the version is compiled into the binary, and the formula's own test asserts that `gtools version` prints the formula's version.

## Relation to 0294

0294 (closed 2026-10-30, landed at 19d87d30) stopped the tests workflow re-running on a tag whose commit is green on `candidate/<tag>`. That candidate exists only under `release.publish.url`, where the snapshot repository's candidate run is the gate. Gtools declares no publish.url, so its 0.8.3 cut skipped snapshot, candidate and publish and ran the other shape: stamp, commit, gates, confirm, tag, push, object, after, then `ci` waiting on the tag's own run. This issue is about that shape, which every estate that cuts without a publish repository uses.

## The fix: stamp first, test once, tag what passed

1. The release core makes the version commit first, with no tag, and pushes it.
2. That one commit gets the test runs: one CI run that includes macOS, plus the kovacs run.
3. The cut tags that exact commit once it is green. Its `gates` step checks the recorded green for that sha instead of running again. Its `ci` step finds the green run whose headSha is the tag's commit, so 0052's guarantee holds (the tagged commit has a green CI run). The tag's own run skips its legs on that green, as 0294's Candidate verdict job does for a candidate branch.

That is one run per platform per release, on the commit that ships. A workflow that builds or publishes release assets on a tag (Intent's linux-release.yml, Conflab's release.yml) still runs on the tag; only the test legs stop running there.

## hv's constraints, 2026-10-30

- Keep the kovacs run: "No, I don't want to avoid the kovacs tests because its quicker than the CI/CD to find issues and there have been _multiple_ stupid missed errors on the Linux build that cost _hours_ in retesting."
- Not tonight, and not soon: "But the rest, yes, but defiitely not tonight. We can raise the issue with devbin and then come back to it next time we make a devbin release, which will not be any time soon, unless it's absolutely necessary."

## Reach

Utilz, Intent, Gtools, Laksa and Conflab each vendor this release core (bin/.devbin/lib/cmd/release), so each takes the fix with its next vendor update. The test workflows that also run on a tag push are Utilz's tests.yml, Intent's rust.yml and tests.yml, and Gtools' ci.yml (whose macOS job reads `if: ${{ github.ref_type == 'tag' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' }}`). Each project changes its own triggers when it takes the new devbin.

Filed by intent-vc on hv's word, from intent-vc's session.

Resolution (cc, 2026-11-01 18:46Z by date -u): fixed by ST0011's cut, with no code of its own; vc's triage of 2026-11-01 18:43Z. The three steps of the fix above, as built:
1. The version commit first, with no tag, pushed. The cut confirms once, then stamps and commits the release commit R and pushes R to candidate/<tag>. No tag is made before every leg is green (ST0011/02a bd13167f, ST0011/02b ac18a7de).
2. That one commit gets the test runs. Every leg runs on R under one wait: the local gates; CI's run on the candidate at R's sha, the whole matrix where the test workflow runs its macOS jobs on candidate/ branches, as Devbin's does; the remote legs release.legs declares, kovacs among them, which hv's constraint above keeps; and the macOS stage at R where the project declares one (ST0011/05 7333cae0 and ee5791e5, ST0011/06 314f3c78).
3. The tag goes on that exact commit once every leg is green. A sealed green for R on its platform stands, so a re-run does not run the gates again (ST0011/01 bc744227). The ci step, ci.tag and ci.base are retired, and CI's verdict is read on R's sha through the built-in ci-state (ST0011/03 76a0fba6 and ebc38b18), so the tagged commit is the commit CI passed and 0052's guarantee holds by construction. No tag starts a run of Devbin's tests workflow; release.yml still builds the release object on the tag (ST0011/04 a4238ca6).

WP02c makes the candidate leg every cut's default: release.ci.query is the built-in unless a project opts out (ST0011/02c 16e83e18). Each consumer changes its own test workflow's triggers when it takes this release core (ST0011 WP10 to WP14, AC-4.3). The cut's push of main still starts main's own Ubuntu check of the published branch on R, which the cut does not wait for: AC-4.1 as amended on 2026-11-01.
